23.88000,55.17000.name: Information Notice with regard to the detected GM zebrafish (Danio rerio) in the Republic of Lithuania
23.88000,55.17000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
23.88000,55.17000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-89.98680,38.56620.name: Kindbody Fertility Institute-St Louis
-89.98680,38.56620.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Amber Cooper, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

77.12684,28.70672.name: Fetal Medicine & Child Clinic
77.12684,28.70672.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

0.07788,51.64904.name: CREATE Fertility Loughton
0.07788,51.64904.state: CREATE Fertility Loughton, Rectory Lane, Loughton, IG10 3RU
0.07788,51.64904.company: Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, London St Paul's
0.07788,51.64904.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, London St Paul's. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-123.23329,49.34058.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025
-123.23329,49.34058.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. A site of Fisheries and Oceans Canada. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-71.54763,-16.39825.name: INBIOFER - Instituto de Biomedicina y Fertilidad - ClÃ­nica Melo
-71.54763,-16.39825.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

8.42900,49.49800.name: BASF Agricultural Solutions
8.42900,49.49800.desc: The fourth of the companies that dominate world seed and crop protection, and the one with the smallest seed business relative to its chemistry. It bought the vegetable seed and hybrid wheat lines Bayer was forced to divest as a condition of the Monsanto acquisition, so a competition remedy is what gave it the position it now holds. Its herbicide-tolerance systems are licensed into other companies' varieties, which is the usual arrangement: the trait and the seed it travels in are frequently owned by different firms, and a farmer buying one is paying both.

-117.03800,32.51500.name: Cross-border stem cell clinics
-117.03800,32.51500.desc: Clinics in Mexico, Panama, the Caribbean and parts of Asia sell unapproved cell treatments to patients who travel for them, often after exhausting options at home. Regulatory arbitrage in medicine works the same way as in agriculture: the jurisdiction is chosen, not the treatment.

90.39930,23.77700.name: National Committee on Biosafety (Bangladesh)
90.39930,23.77700.state: Dhaka — Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
90.39930,23.77700.desc: Bangladesh's apex biosafety authority, and the body that in November 2013 cleared Bt brinjal for commercial cultivation — the first approval of an edible engineered crop anywhere in South Asia, granted while the identical event remained blocked next door in India. A regulator's decisions are usually read against its own country's law. This one is more usefully read against the region's: where two neighbouring states hold the same dossier and reach opposite conclusions, the dossier is not what decided it.

121.50000,31.23720.name: Qiming Venture Partners
121.50000,31.23720.state: Shanghai — Jin Mao Tower, with Beijing, Suzhou, Hong Kong and Singapore
121.50000,31.23720.desc: Founded in 2006 and managing around $9.5 billion across eleven dollar funds and seven renminbi funds, investing in technology, consumer and healthcare companies with more than 500 investments made. Its healthcare portfolio includes gene editing companies working on genetic disease and mRNA drug developers, and in 2017 it launched a US team and fund of its own. Two structural points: a fund running parallel dollar and renminbi vehicles can take money from foreign and domestic investors into different pools with different rules, which is how Chinese biotechnology has been financed from both directions at once; and a Chinese venture firm raising in the United States is the reverse of the flow this map usually records.
